posts.name: OddballPaladin
posts.cooked:
Seems like Choke/Chokepoint is easy enough to retcon as an Omega, even if there wasn’t enough time passing. Sure, she “heard” the metal… but it was all in her head until her encounter with Isoflux Alpha.

I think I got the additive/multiplying strength bit. I also agree with A&C that it’s a bit weirder than trying to math it out. On the one hand, in the RPG stats Legacy has a lower Strength die than Heritage, but to me that just means she’s not as used to applying the strength as her father. If we were using a crunchier system, I would likely have their physical stats equal.

Plus, strength is hard to measure with flying heroes, because you have the question of strength vs leverage. I imagine Wearing the Cape is at least known to others on this board, but in that there is a bit of a comparison between the flying brick types (say, Legacy) and more “conventional” super strength types (like Haka or Fright Train), where even if they have equal strength in terms of lifting, the flying brick types are better able to flat out move stuff (or send opponents flying into the sky like Team Rocket) because they can apply their flight ability.

(Yes, I’ve given this a lot of thought… I’m a SFF writer, and one of my projects is a superhero novel… Granted, my main character in there isn’t a flyer, but she is a portal-based teleporter and I have her pulling tricks straight out of Portal.)

Actually, I suspect that Legacy might be viewed as being STRONGER than Heritage. Because while they’re probably about equal in the great feats (preventing building collapse, and similar), Felicia always struck me as more impulsive and direct than her father, so maybe she’s demonstrated that kind of strength through punching things through walls more often than her predecessor.

posts.cooked: When C&A were discussing a villain that was just a friendly, low-grade fan (as opposed to Radioactivist-levels of creepy) who happened to be fighting against Legacy, I was really hoping that would end up being one of her major nemeses. Sort of like the opposite of the Tachyon / Glamour relationship, where this bad is just very impressed by Legacy and chats a lot and compliments her on her fighting style, but is still amoral enough to just go ahead with the evil plan anyway, and it drives Legacy up the wall because this guy seems nice but he IS HURTING PEOPLE and will not admit that it’s a problem.

posts.cooked:
Apparently Adam defines the Celestial Tribunal as being an actual sword, just because it looks like one. (Especially if you put Baron Ivan Ramonat on the Tribunal, because then the sword has a Blade on it.)

The notion of a Young Legacy super fan who becomes a villain is similar to the Radioactivist in concept, but I think if you just make it a girl, that’s enough to make it an interestingly different character. Even if she’s being full on Single White Female, she wouldn’t scan as being a gross creep that just makes the heroine go “ugh!” when she shows up. It’d also be neat to make this character obsessively committing crimes because YL will show up and stop her, a very Professor Zoom kind of relationship.

Random thought that happened to crop up while listening to this episode…is Iron Legacy a servant of Gloomweaver by default? He doubtless kills all sorts of Cult of Gloom members, but it’s not like Gloomy values those; IL is himself totally lost to despair, he causes terror and grief worldwide by constantly oppressing everyone, I think he could smash every relic to powder and throw Ophidia into the sun, and Gloomweaver would still be the strongest he’s ever been with IL as functionally his entire cult.

I’ve decided that Citizen Dawn has a couple of non-combatant Citizens named Ways and Means.

C&A like to rely heavily on archetypes, especially with high school and college students. I think that there ought to be a plurality of adolescents who would take offense at being classified into some broadly cliched tropes. Somebody who doesn’t want people parsing them as a jock or a nerd or a goth or a preppie, they just want to be themselves, and every time they get stereotyped they just get a bigger and bigger chip on their shoulder about it.

Mathlete wins all the guessing games … until he goes to MM’s.

Professor Stabbington

Where in the world is Carman San Diego?

Most of this Gruum letter wasn’t my favorite, but I really loved the final run-on sentence, that part was top notch.

To me the eggnapping story is really neat, albeit a little skin-crawling, but only gets interesting with one added wrinkle: this stuff happens and a biological child is created, then Felecia has a child in the more family-friendly way, the young Mx. Fields gets the Legacy powers, and then the eggnap child shows up and gains the powers instead. So now you have evil powered child of Legacy AND power-lost inheritor of the mentle, both becoming villains who hate each other.

C&A didn’t call any attention to the fact that the Cult of Gloom letter slid in Take Down as part of their otherwise classic sign off. I enjoyed the subtlety.

So the villain Choke is literally a baby who was thrown out with the bathwater…

I think this is my longest episode response ever, at least as LonelyMan. It’s been a long time since I had anywhere near this many things to comment on, even if a couple of the comments are kinda off topic. I got one am rather glad that’s not being policed anymore, in the matter that created the Justifications thread.
